title: Redwood Console - Tracing + Request Logs Debugging Walkthrough

Share SOC2 + ISO27001 security pack and KMS integration guide
Run a 48hr benchmark on their staging workload and share results
Follow up with pricing for Dedicated capacity and pilot proposal
action_items: Maya Chen: Send recording + security docs (due: 2028-03-14)
Ravi Patel: Run sample trace + request-log export for Vertex staging (due: 2028-03-16)
Leah Gomez: Provide representative request template and expected error cases (due: 2028-03-15)
transcript:
Header: 2028-03-12 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Park (Product), Leah Gomez (Vertex Platform Eng), Derek Wu (Vertex SRE), Nina Alvarez (Vertex Head of ML), Samir Patel (Vertex Security)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing, error analysis, and request logs for debugging production regressions; validated SSO/KMS questions; agreed next steps for benchmark and security docs.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we're gonna walk through the console tracing and request logs today, show how you'd debug a flakey inference issue and what artifacts we provide.
00:12 Leah Gomez: thanks, excited — we've been seeing random 500-ish errors when we hit higher qps, so want to see how you surface root causes.
00:20 Ravi Patel: yeah great, we'll start with a quick trace demo then hop into request logs and the error analysis flows, and then time for questions.
01:01 Derek Wu: just to call out we run a mix of hosted and some Dedicated capacity — currently prod is hosted, we have a dedicated pool coming for compliance.
01:15 Maya Chen: perfect, that helps — we'll show policy-based routing and how fallbacks are logged.

02:05 [Screen shares start — console opened]
02:12 Ravi Patel: ok up top is the Traces tab, you can filter by model, route, trace id, duration, status — note there's a live sampling rate which we can tune.
02:29 Nina Alvarez: sampling rate — does that affect KV cache visibility? like if we sample 1% do we still see kv cache hits?
02:38 Ravi Patel: good question — sampling controls trace capture; request logs still retain full metadata for the retention window, but large payloads may be redacted depending on retention settings. KV cache hits are shown when the trace is captured; otherwise request logs have hit/miss counters.

04:00 Derek Wu: can we see the actual prompt and tokens in the trace? we need to reproduce errors with exact input.
04:10 Ravi Patel: by default PII and long prompts are redacted; we have field-level redaction and you can enable secure-logging with customer-managed KMS to keep full payloads for a period. Needs SOC2+KMS config which Samir can confirm.
04:28 Samir Patel: yes we have to confirm legal for that, but ok.

06:20 Ravi Patel: here's an example trace: request -> router -> model shard -> runtime. You can see per-stage latencies, kernel selection notes (we'll sometimes show when quantized kernels are used), and any fallback events.
06:45 Maya Chen: note the orange bar there is the fallback to a smaller model variant because burst capacity exceeded SLA, we log the reason and the configured fallback policy.
07:10 Leah Gomez: ah that explains a spike we saw on Friday where responses slowed then errors started — maybe fallback triggered and some requests timed out.

09:00 [15s pause, typing]
09:20 Ravi Patel: moving on to Error Analysis view — it's built on top of traces and request logs; we group by error signature and provide sample request ids that you can click to open the full trace.
09:35 Derek Wu: do you do automatic fingerprinting of errors across versions? we have model rollouts and regressions are a big worry.
09:44 Oliver Park: yes we tie errors to model versions and rollout windows; you can compare error rates by model tag and by route over time, and we surface regressions tied to eval prompt sets if you upload them.

11:05 Nina Alvarez: is there a way to export all failed requests for offline analysis?
11:12 Ravi Patel: yep CSV/Parquet exports from request logs; you can filter to error code, latency bucket, model, and time range. Also streaming export to your S3/GCS for long-term retention.
11:30 Leah Gomez: retention — what's default? how long are traces vs request logs kept?
11:35 Maya Chen: default traces are 30 days sampled, request logs 90 days, but enterprise plans can extend retention and we offer long-term archival to customer's cloud.

13:50 Derek Wu: quick question on SLOs — can we set alerts on trace-derived latency percentiles?
13:58 Ravi Patel: yes alerts can be set on p50/p95/p99 from traces and request logs; we also support anomaly detection tied to your baseline.

15:30 [showing an example failure chain]
15:40 Ravi Patel: here a request timed out at the runtime in the kernel selection step — note the stack trace and the runtime error code 0x7c (this is transcribed; actual code label might be different in UI). We also show downstream retry attempts and whether they hit cache.
15:58 Leah Gomez: great, in our logs we saw a lot of retries that correlated with pod restarts. can you show how restarts surface in traces?
16:08 Ravi Patel: sure — we log instance health events; traces will show a node-level meta entry like instance-id and last-health-check. If a restart happened mid-request it's visible as a warning marker.

18:10 Maya Chen: for private deployments we also collect host-level syslogs if enabled, and link them to traces in the console for pivoting to infra signals.

20:00 [customer asks about debugging flow]
20:05 Leah Gomez: so if we get a regression, what's the recommended triage sequence?
20:12 Ravi Patel: we usually recommend: 1) look at Error Analysis to group and find top signatures, 2) open sample trace to see failure stage and timings, 3) export request logs for bulk analysis, 4) compare model version metrics and rollout windows, 5) run replay on a staging Dedicated pool.
20:28 Nina Alvarez: replay — how deterministic is replay? we need to ensure we can reproduce the same KV state.
20:35 Ravi Patel: replay simulates request payloads and can optionally warm KV cache with recorded prefixes; we provide a replay harness that attempts to match sequence length and cache state but absolute determinism depends on external state and dynamic model components.

23:00 Derek Wu: what about redaction & compliance — we need to keep everything in-house for HIPAA-type workloads.
23:10 Maya Chen: for HIPAA we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; request logs can be kept in your cloud and we can restrict console access via SAML + RBAC.
23:34 Samir Patel: ok we'll take notes, can you send the KMS setup doc.

25:20 [Ravi navigates to Request Logs UI]
25:30 Ravi Patel: Request logs are event-first — each row is a request id with timestamp, model, route, latency, status, error_code, shard_id, instance_id, cache_hit boolean, and a link to traces when available. You can also search free text across prompts if allowed by retention settings.
25:52 Leah Gomez: can I run an ad-hoc query with regex across prompts?
25:58 Ravi Patel: yes we support basic regex and field filters; heavy queries can be offloaded to the export pipeline.

28:40 Nina Alvarez: how do you surface noisy downstream dependencies — like third-party tokenizers failing — do those appear in traces?
28:48 Ravi Patel: yes for integrated tool calls or tokenizer services we instrument calls and include them as spans; if an external call fails it appears in trace timeline with the error and latency.

31:00 Maya Chen: demo time — here's a real example they provided with intermittent 500s; I'll filter to the route and time window you gave.
31:12 [Console filters applied]
31:30 Ravi Patel: see these clustered errors at 14:03 — open sample trace: you can see kernel selection took longer due to a suboptimal kernel on the node, then a timeout.
31:50 Derek Wu: kernel selection — is that influenced by sequence length heuristics? our customers push variable lengths.
31:58 Ravi Patel: yes heuristics choose kernels by sequence length distribution; long tails can cause occasional mis-selection, we do per-instance heuristics and recommend profiling with Optimize to pick quantization or kernel profiles for your workload.

34:10 Leah Gomez: is Optimize integrated with Console? can it auto-suggest quantization profiles?
34:18 Oliver Park: yes Optimize will analyze token distribution and recommend quantization and batching profiles; you can apply those profiles to a Dedicated pool or test them on a shadow pool.

36:00 [minor crosstalk]
36:20 Ravi Patel: next I want to show how to create a debugging workspace — you can pin a trace set, save queries, and assign to an incident. Each incident collects traces, logs, and timeline notes for post-mortem.
36:40 Nina Alvarez: can incidents be exported to Jira/Slack?
36:46 Maya Chen: yes integrations: Slack alerts, Jira export, and webhooks.

38:55 Derek Wu: question on RBAC — can we create a role that only sees redacted request logs but full traces for security team?
39:03 Maya Chen: we have fine-grained roles; yes you can create roles with 'view-redacted-logs' and 'view-full-traces-with-kms' which requires the KMS key access; access requests are audited.

41:20 Samir Patel: about audit logs — do you provide immutable audit trails? we need to show changes to fallback policies and who ran a replay.
41:30 Ravi Patel: yes audit logs capture console actions, policy changes, replay runs, and exports. For Private, we can forward to your SIEM.

43:45 Leah Gomez: one more on latency — we saw sudden p99 spikes, are there ways to correlate with autoscaler events?
43:54 Ravi Patel: autoscaler activity is emitted as infra events and linked in traces; you can overlay autoscaler up/down events on latency charts to correlate.

46:10 [Ravi demonstrates request log export]
46:20 Ravi Patel: export includes request_id, timestamp, route, model_version, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, status, error_code, cache_hit, instance_id; if you enable secure payload retention it will include full prompt and response columns.
46:44 Derek Wu: can we mask certain fields for contractors?
46:50 Maya Chen: yes masking rules and field-level RBAC — you can define patterns to mask PII before export.

48:30 Nina Alvarez: about cost — storing full request logs for 1 year might be expensive; any compression or downsampling strategies?
48:40 Oliver Park: we recommend tiered retention: full payloads for 30-90 days, compact metadata longer; we also support deduplication and delta-compression for repeated requests. Optimize can recommend retention policies based on usage.

50:15 Maya Chen: ok quick recap — we demonstrated traces, error analysis grouping, request log exports, incidents, and integrations; we answered SSO/KMS/RBAC questions and agreed to run a 48hr benchmark in staging.

51:00 Leah Gomez: thanks this was super helpful — we'll share the sample requests and give access to a staging cluster for the benchmark.
51:12 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll send recording and security docs and get the benchmark queued.
51:20 Derek Wu: one more tiny ask — can you also share a quick runbook for triage steps?
51:25 Ravi Patel: yes will include a one-page triage runbook in the follow-up.

52:00 [Meeting ends with small goodbyes]

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcribed tokens and some product names may be slightly off (e.g., kernel identifiers); speakers sometimes overlap.
